_rule: An order's work is finished IFF at least one of its tasks is COMPLETED. Nothing else finishes it: not a date, not a cancellation, not the absence of tasks.
_why: TODO-41. This rule is written three times, in two languages, with no shared code: OrderRepository.findLiveBySubscriptionId (JPQL) refuses to retire a subscription while an unfinished order points at it; TaskService.summariseOrderTasks rolls an order's tasks up for GET /api/tasks/order/{id}/exists; isOrderFulfilled (web) splits Comenzi into Curente and Arhivă. TODO-40's doc_claims.py pins that they keep NAMING each other. This file is what pins that they still AGREE.

_fields.taskStatuses: The order's tasks, in the order the API returns them (id ascending). All unscheduled, so the summary cannot be decided by a date.
_fields.summarisedStatus: What GET /tasks/order/{id}/exists must report for that order: COMPLETED if any task is, else the first task's status, else null for an order with no tasks.
_fields.fulfilled: Whether the order is finished — i.e. it belongs in Arhivă, and no longer blocks retiring its subscription.
_fields.backendOnly: Set when the case uses a status the web app has no name for. The web TaskStatus union is NEW/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED; CANCELLED is backend-only, as cross_project_invariants.py declares. The web suite skips these; the backend suite runs everything.

cases.name: no task at all — never carried out, so never finished
two tasks, the LAST completed — the disagreement TODO-34 fixed
two tasks, the FIRST completed — position must not decide either
work started but not finished, then a second attempt completed it
cancelled and re-done — the completion still decides
